title: How to add variations/rotations to your Gentleman split
summary: NH defines variations (lifts that feed a main lift, used sparingly as replacements or additions) and rotations (lifts that alternate in the same slot week to week, ideally the same movement pattern), and explains autoregulated rotations. His advice is to keep it simple: use A/B rotations of the same pattern, keep strength work regular, and master variations before rotations. He closes with a back squat example.
claims: Variations and rotations are scheduled changes to movement patterns that keep progression going; there is nothing magical about either
A variation implies a main lift it varies from, so you need a specificity tree before you can talk about variations
Novices can use variations too instead of repeating the identical lift three times a week, as long as they stay very close in specificity; advanced lifters can be more exotic
Any lift can be a variation; the back squat is normally a main lift simply because it does that job so well
Use variations like jokers, only with a good reason such as breaking a stall or fixing technique (for example pause squats for the bottom position)
Build any good program around the lifts first, then set volume, intensity and frequency; choosing a 5x5 and then a lift is backwards
Main lifts open the day as strength work; variations are for accumulating tonnage and should progress more slowly than the main lift
One variation can feed several main lifts, for example good mornings feed both squat and deadlift; every lift in a program is connected
Rotations alternate lifts in the same slot week to week (week A vs week B) and should use the same movement pattern, or the program needs compensating work elsewhere
Rotations that don't share a pattern multiply the bookkeeping (2 becomes 4, then 8); beginners should avoid them
Rotations prevent overuse injuries and add freshness and flexibility to a program
Autoregulation means choosing on the day, and it needs mechanisms built into the program, such as a menu of rotation options
His own sessions contain 4-5 hours of options; he picks 4-5 sets of mostly supersets each day based on last and next week
Past a certain amount of volume, progression should come from intensity and program complexity rather than more sets
Keep rotations to a simple A/B and don't put them in strength work at first; strength work needs to be regular
Master variations before using rotations, and don't build a complex program six months in
Minimalism is neither good nor bad; it only becomes a problem when it stops your progress
If the back squat stalls, either replace one of three weekly sessions with a variation (Wednesday pause squats) or add the variation; a variation can also come before the main lift
Example rotation: alternate pause squats one week with Zercher squats the next while keeping back squats three times a week
